subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: To Kill a Mockingbird and Racial Justice
description: A fast breakdown of To Kill a Mockingbird and Racial Justice for builders.

hook.text: Harper Lee published one novel in 1960, and it became one of the most influential books in American history.

buildup.text: To Kill a Mockingbird told the story of a Black man falsely accused of a crime in the Deep South.

discovery.text: Narrated through a child's innocent eyes, the novel forced white readers to confront systemic racism.

twist.text: Despite winning the Pulitzer Prize, many Southern schools banned the book for decades.

climax.text: The novel inspired a generation of lawyers and activists who fought for civil rights in America.

punchline.text: A child narrator taught adults about justice.

quiz.question: Why was To Kill a Mockingbird so impactful?
options: It was the longest novel ever published
It forced readers to confront racism through a child's perspective
It documented real court cases accurately
